sector: An independent clean beauty house running a prestige apothecary skincare line at counter and a mass everyday colour line on peg.
founded_place_size: A small independent clean beauty house in Portland, Oregon, launching nineteen SKUs across two lines this autumn.
about: SEVE Botanicals makes clean, plant led beauty under one house across two very different shelves. Seve Atelier is the apothecary line, sold over a counter, where restraint and an honest ingredient line are the proof of quality. Seve Everyday is the drugstore line on a peg, where a shade has to win in four seconds. Same mark, same values, two registers.
audience: Two buyers under one house: a thirty to fifty five year old counter customer paying for restraint and reading the ingredient list as proof, and a sixteen to thirty five year old drugstore shopper scanning a peg for a shade at arm's length.
price_positioning: Two load bearing tiers. Seve Atelier runs 48 to 85 dollars: quiet, generous negative space, one considered accent, the mark small and confident, the swatch a single honest chip. Seve Everyday runs 6 to 14 dollars: claim forward and shade forward, the shade name and swatch winning at arm's length, the mark holding while small and busy. The same treatment cannot serve both.
typography: A modern editorial pairing that holds across an 85 dollar counter serum and a 6 dollar peg tint without either tier borrowing the other's register: a refined high contrast or clean serif for the wordmark and shade names, with a clear humanist sans for ingredient lines, net weight and batch fields where legibility at small size is critical. Note that no chosen face can reach the printed label, which keeps the label printer's typography.
voice: Calm, botanical and precise, never gushing. Compliance copy stays exactly as written. Example line the brand would write: "One house, two shelves, every shade drawn from the real product."
brand_assets_status: The wordmark was drawn years ago by a designer the house has lost touch with and survives only foil blocked on an old carton, with no dark version at all. The only layout owned is last season's serum label as the flat press PDF the label printer returned. Photography is minimal: one physical sample bottle shot on a phone on kitchen marble, plus nineteen shade drawdowns done on card by the window the same afternoon.
values: Honesty on the shelf: the swatch is the real shade, the ingredient line is exactly as compliance wrote it, and each tier must look right at its own price while staying recognisably one house.
